title: Add editable manufacturer and supplier references to network settings and plan cartouches

needs: Enter one manufacturer plan reference and one supplier plan reference in network parameters.
Edit the company name associated with each reference independently; company names must not be fixed labels.
Show both references and their associated company names in exported plan cartouches.
context: User request on 2026-10-23 against repository version 1.21.0. This chain scopes development only; no runtime implementation is requested in this change. Documents use English; UI copy supports EN/FR.

Scope decision: these are references identifying the network plan as a whole. They are unrelated to connector/catalog manufacturerReference, wire endpoint material references, BOM references, network technicalId, projectCode or planRevision. Exactly two fixed semantic roles are required: manufacturer and supplier.

Interpretation of editable company labels: each role contains a company name and a reference value, giving four editable text inputs in total. Names belong to the network and are user data. Documentation and fixtures use Manufacturer A and Supplier B as anonymized examples. No real company name or brand-specific default is introduced.

Network already stores optional author/projectCode/exportNotes/planRevision/planIssueDate. networkMetadata, networkClone, networkReducer, migrations and networkFile normalize explicit metadata allowlists. Follow and extend the existing complete path rather than storing local-only UI values.

The existing network create/edit flow is shared by NetworkScopeWorkspaceContent, networkFormDraft, form state/orchestration and useWorkspaceHandlers. Follow its submit/cancel, draft reset, network switching and historical read-only behavior.

The cartouche is generated in networkSummaryExport, with parameters supplied through controller, panel types and export actions. Existing metadata rows are omitted when empty and cartouche width is capped; long new text requires wrapping and measured height. Inspect preview and any existing PDF consumer of the same export renderer without creating a new export flow.

prod_022 remains the reference for issue revision/date semantics. This focused brief adds business identification to the same per-network metadata model without changing release or workspace history semantics.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Store four optional per-Network text values: planManufacturerName, planManufacturerReference, planSupplierName and planSupplierReference. Manufacturer/supplier are fixed roles; both names and both reference values are independently editable and clearable. Each accepts trimmed single-line Unicode text, names up to 80 characters and reference codes up to 120 characters; preserve case, internal spaces, punctuation and leading zeroes. Empty/whitespace-only values are unset. Interactive input prevents over-limit values and reports invalid multiline input; shared normalization removes non-string values and sanitizes imported line breaks to spaces with bounded lengths. Do not reuse the project-code character restriction or entity-prefix formatter.

AC2: Network create/edit parameters expose two clearly grouped roles with accessible EN/FR labels: manufacturer company name/reference and supplier company name/reference. All four inputs are optional, including name-only and reference-only combinations. Use generic placeholders, never hardcoded real company names. Saving updates only the target network; cancel, reopen, reset and switching networks do not leak drafts. Existing network save validation and historical read-only gates apply. Changes take the ordinary metadata dirty/save and undo/redo path without rerouting or changing entity technical IDs.

AC3: All four values survive create/update, duplicate/clone, undo/redo, application reload, browser/folder workspace save/open, portable workspace Copy, stored lineage versions and network export/import including import-conflict paths. Audit every explicit metadata allowlist and serializer. Existing files with no fields remain valid with all values unset; malformed imported optional values follow shared normalization and existing import-warning conventions without dropping the network or unrelated data. Choose any schema/version adjustment under existing portability policy. Frozen versions retain their captured values and cannot be changed by later working-copy edits.

AC4: When the identity cartouche is enabled, each non-empty role produces a distinct localized manufacturer/supplier row using the exported network values. With both values present, show Manufacturer (Manufacturer A): MFG-001 and Supplier (Supplier B): SUP-009 in English and equivalent French role labels; company names/reference values themselves are never translated. With only the reference, show the generic role and reference; with only the company name, show the role and company name without a dangling separator. Omit a role only when both values are unset. Preserve manufacturer-before-supplier order and existing metadata rows/toggle behavior. Editing a name replaces it in subsequent exports without changing either reference.

AC5: Propagate the four values through all existing preview/export parameter paths. SVG and PNG plus any existing PDF path consuming that renderer show matching role/name/reference values from the correct network, with no stale data after edits or network switches. Measure/wrap long company names and reference codes, including unbroken 120-character codes; expand cartouche height and export bounds as needed so rows, logo and notes remain readable without clipping or overlap at supported sizes. XML-sensitive characters and non-Latin text remain literal safe text. Disabled cartouches emit none of these rows; exports do not mutate metadata or dirty/history state.

AC6: Add meaningful targeted normalization/form/reducer/portability and export regressions: distinct values on two networks, independent edits/clears, all partial/empty combinations, whitespace, bounds, imported wrong types/line breaks, clone, undo/redo, legacy-file roundtrips, workspace/network serialization and frozen history. Cover EN/FR labels, submit/cancel/switch behavior, long cartouche content with logo/notes and cartouche disabled, SVG text plus PNG/shared-renderer propagation. Reuse existing plan-issue fixtures and relevant lineage tests rather than duplicating whole test suites.

AC7: Document the two plan-level roles, editable company names, optional-value/cartouche rules and scope difference from component references in the appropriate existing network/export help, creating a focused help page only if none exists. Record per-AC implementation/test evidence in the orchestration task. Before implementation closeout run applicable lint, typecheck, i18n, targeted tests, build and repository-required delivery gates. This corpus alone stays ready for development and does not claim runtime delivery.

product.title: Editable manufacturer and supplier identification on network plans
product.overview: Identify a network plan using two independent business reference codes with editable company names, maintained in network parameters and rendered consistently in plan cartouches.
goals: Support one manufacturer and one supplier reference per network.
Allow users to change both associated company names without changing role semantics.
Keep saved, portable and exported plan identification consistent across networks and versions.
non_goals: Arbitrary additional reference roles, multiple suppliers or company directories.
Catalog/contact/BOM reference changes, automatic lookup or synchronization with external companies.
Release approvals, automatic reference numbering, global company defaults or a new export format.
Runtime implementation or release publication in this documentation change.

backlog_items.title: Persist per-network manufacturer and supplier plan reference metadata
problem: The Network model has no fields for role-specific plan references or editable company names; explicit normalization allowlists can lose newly added fields.
scope_in: Add the four optional Network fields with shared trim/length/single-line normalization and form-compatible validation. Preserve reference codes as strings.
Extend actions, reducers, metadata updates, clone/import helpers, migrations and network/workspace portability paths. Preserve ordinary metadata history/dirty behavior and legacy compatibility.

Verify two-network isolation, partial clears, omitted-versus-explicit-clear update behavior, clone, undo/redo, malformed imports, network/workspace roundtrips and frozen version isolation. Record mapped AC evidence.
scope_out: UI layout, rendering cartouches and component/material reference changes.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Request AC1 and AC3 pass through canonical metadata and portability paths without cross-network contamination.
AC2: Targeted data/history/compatibility evidence covers the corresponding AC6 cases and contributes to AC7.

backlog_items.title: Edit manufacturer and supplier company names and references in network parameters
problem: Users cannot enter the two plan reference codes or customize the associated company names in network create/edit forms.
scope_in: Extend existing network form drafts, hooks, orchestration, handlers and shared create/edit controls with two role groups and four accessible optional inputs. Use generic EN/FR labels and placeholders.

Apply shared validation, optional/partial rules, max lengths and existing submit/cancel/read-only behavior. Ensure reloading drafts or switching networks cannot carry one network company identity into another.

Add focused interaction tests for editing each name separately from its reference, create/save/reopen, clear, partial values, cancel and switching; document parameter semantics and record AC evidence.
scope_out: Global Settings company presets, company catalogs and extra reference roles.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Request AC2 works using AC1 data rules with EN/FR and existing network edit/read-only semantics.
AC2: UI evidence covers the applicable AC6 cases and user documentation supports AC7.

backlog_items.title: Render manufacturer and supplier plan references in export cartouches
problem: Current cartouches cannot identify either business reference or its editable associated company, and capped metadata rows need wrapping for long values.
scope_in: Thread all four values from the exported network through controller slices, panel props, preview and export actions to the shared cartouche renderer. Follow any existing PNG/PDF consumer.

Render localized fixed roles with literal editable names/references, deterministic partial/empty behavior and safe text nodes. Wrap/measure long values and adjust row heights/cartouche bounds while preserving logo, notes and toggle behavior.

Verify two-network/export freshness, EN/FR, name edits, all empty/partial combinations, long Unicode/XML-sensitive text, logo/notes and SVG/PNG parity. Finish export help and complete per-request AC evidence and applicable delivery checks.
scope_out: A new PDF workflow, BOM columns and unrelated export redesign.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Request AC4-AC5 pass for all existing consumers of the shared cartouche renderer.
AC2: Applicable AC6 export tests and AC7 documentation/quality evidence are recorded before implementation closeout.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver editable network manufacturer and supplier references in plan cartouches
plan: Wave 1: Deliver metadata normalization, actions/reducers, clone/import and persistence/portability contracts; establish asymmetric two-network fixtures and prove AC1/AC3 including legacy and frozen-version behavior.

Wave 2: Deliver the network create/edit role groups and all four independent inputs using the shared contract. Verify draft/reset/cancel/switch behavior, optional combinations, EN/FR and read-only gates; record AC2 evidence.

Wave 3: Deliver controller-to-export propagation and localized cartouche rows, partial-value formatting and measured wrapping/bounds. Verify shared SVG/PNG and existing PDF consumers, disabled cartouches and stale-data prevention; record AC4-AC5 evidence.

Wave 4: Complete AC6 regression coverage, focused user help, per-AC traceability and applicable lint/typecheck/i18n/build/repository delivery gates for AC7. Use lifecycle commands for progress and closeout only after implementation and evidence exist.

All three backlog slices have Medium priority because this is an additive plan-identification feature with no reported blocking defect. Data contract comes first; forms and export can follow it independently. This scoping chain remains unimplemented.
